metadata.title: AI Distributed Training - Sources
metadata.description: Curated mid-2026 sources for distributed LLM pre-training: FlashAttention 1/2/3, DeepSpeed ZeRO, PyTorch FSDP2, Megatron-LM/Core, DeepSeek-V3 (DualPipe/EP/fp8), Ring Attention (context parallel), Muon/MuonClip (Kimi K2, DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5), torchtitan, pre-training frameworks (litgpt, nanotron), GPT-2 reproduction projects, rented GPU provider docs, and storage/dataloader I/O (Fregly Ch.5, GPUDirect Storage, DALI, 3FS), and hardware fault tolerance / checkpoint-interval reliability (Reddi MLSysBook Ch.16).

research_papers.name: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
research_papers.relevance: Foundational paper introducing FlashAttention — O(N) memory attention via tiled SRAM recomputation. Essential reference for understanding memory-efficient attention at pre-training scale.

research_papers.name: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
research_papers.relevance: FlashAttention-2 improvements: better thread-block partitioning, 2x speedup over v1. Current default for A100/H100 pre-training.

research_papers.name: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models
research_papers.relevance: Primary ZeRO paper describing stages 1, 2, and 3 optimizer/gradient/parameter sharding. Canonical reference for DeepSpeed ZeRO design.

research_papers.name: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism
research_papers.relevance: Foundational paper for tensor parallelism in transformers (column/row parallel linear layers). Basis for all Megatron-style 3-D parallelism implementations.

research_papers.name: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-precision
research_papers.relevance: Hopper-specific (H100) attention: warp-specialization, async, and fp8 attention. Current state of the art for memory-efficient attention on H100/Blackwell.

research_papers.name: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
research_papers.relevance: Landmark efficient-training reference: DualPipe bidirectional pipeline overlap, cross-node expert parallelism without tensor parallelism, fine-grained fp8 training, auxiliary-loss-free MoE load balancing. Essential for any MoE / frontier-scale distributed training.

research_papers.name: Training Deep Nets with Sublinear Memory Cost (Chen et al. 2016)
research_papers.relevance: Origin of the O(sqrt(n)) gradient-checkpointing result: checkpoint sqrt(n) segments of an n-layer net for one extra forward pass per mini-batch. Cited to keep the sqrt(n)-segment policy distinct from per-transformer-block checkpointing, which gives a constant-factor saving instead.

research_papers.name: Reducing Activation Recomputation in Large Transformer Models
research_papers.relevance: Megatron selective activation checkpointing + sequence parallelism. The canonical reference for activation-memory reduction beyond naive full checkpointing.

research_papers.name: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers for Near-Infinite Context
research_papers.relevance: Foundation for context parallelism: shards the sequence dimension and overlaps blockwise attention with ring communication. Basis for long-context training in torchtitan and Megatron.

research_papers.name: Kimi K2 Technical Report (MuonClip optimizer at 1T-param MoE scale)
research_papers.relevance: Production-scale evidence for the Muon/MuonClip optimizer: 1T-param MoE pre-trained on 15.5T tokens with MuonClip + WSD schedule. Reference for optimizer choice beyond AdamW at scale.

research_papers.name: TorchTitan: One-stop PyTorch native solution for production-ready LLM pre-training
research_papers.relevance: PyTorch-native large-scale pre-training: FSDP2, tensor/context/pipeline parallelism, torch.compile, and fp8 composed in one reference framework. Primary source for modern FSDP2-based recipes.

research_papers.name: Muon is Scalable for LLM Training (Moonshot AI 2025)
research_papers.relevance: Weight-decay + per-parameter update-scale fixes that let Muon train at scale without bespoke tuning. Basis for trillion-param production use (Kimi K2, DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5).

research_papers.name: Pretraining Large Language Models with NVFP4 (NVIDIA 2025)
research_papers.relevance: 12B model on 10T tokens with NVFP4 matching fp8 baseline; MXFP4 needed ~36% more tokens. Source for FP4-training maturity and NVFP4-vs-MXFP4 format choice on Blackwell.

research_papers.name: DeepSeek-V4: Towards Highly Efficient Million-Token Context Intelligence
research_papers.relevance: Primary confirmation that DeepSeek-V4 uses the Muon optimizer for pretraining convergence/stability. Verify exact figures against this report before quoting (recent release, June 2026).

research_papers.name: GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering (Zhipu/Z.ai)
research_papers.relevance: Primary source for GLM-5's Muon usage: describes a per-head 'Muon Split' orthogonalization and a zero-redundancy distributed Muon implementation, building on GLM-4.5's recipe.

research_papers.name: Vijay Janapa Reddi, Machine Learning Systems (MLSysBook, open textbook, Oct 2025) — Ch. 16, Robust AI, §16.4 Hardware Faults
research_papers.relevance: Primary source for references/failure-budget-and-checkpointing.md: transient/permanent/intermittent fault taxonomy, per-device MTBF ranges and the cluster-level compounding arithmetic that drives checkpoint cadence, Table 16.1 fault-tolerance overhead (single/double-bit ECC, TMR, checkpoint-restart), Table 16.2 ECC memory-bandwidth impact, and the silent-data-corruption note for large checkpoints. Tables 16.1/16.2 and the MTBF ranges carry no citation in the textbook — treat as textbook-reported and verify against vendor specs before use.

official_framework_docs.name: PyTorch FSDP Tutorial
official_framework_docs.relevance: Official PyTorch FSDP walkthrough: sharding strategies, mixed precision, checkpointing, and performance tips. Primary reference for FSDP configuration.

official_framework_docs.name: DeepSpeed Documentation
official_framework_docs.relevance: Official DeepSpeed ZeRO config reference: ZeRO stages, offload settings, gradient accumulation, bf16/fp16 config. Authoritative source for DeepSpeed setup.

official_framework_docs.name: Megatron-LM GitHub
official_framework_docs.relevance: NVIDIA's reference implementation for tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism at very large scale. Canonical source for 3-D parallelism configuration and training recipes.

official_framework_docs.name: torchft — per-step fault-tolerant distributed training (PyTorch)
official_framework_docs.relevance: Meta/PyTorch project for per-step fault tolerance: fault-tolerant DDP/HSDP plus LocalSGD/DiLoCo, with a lighthouse coordinator that allows replica-group membership to change at step granularity so a lost node does not force a full-job restart. The 2026 successor to pure checkpoint/restart on large clusters. Verified live 2026-08-31; young and moving — check current API maturity before depending on it.

pretraining_frameworks.name: torchtitan GitHub
pretraining_frameworks.relevance: PyTorch's own reference pre-training framework built on FSDP2, context parallelism, and torch.compile. Actively developed Meta reference for large-scale pre-training.

pretraining_frameworks.name: HuggingFace nanotron GitHub
pretraining_frameworks.relevance: HuggingFace's efficient 3-D parallel pre-training framework. Used for BLOOM and IDEFICS. Supports tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism with a clean config system.

pretraining_frameworks.name: modded-nanoGPT GitHub (Karpathy fork with speed records)
pretraining_frameworks.relevance: Speed-optimized nanoGPT fork. Reference for GPT-2 124M reproduction with minimal code. Holds community speed records; excellent for benchmarking training throughput.

pretraining_frameworks.name: llm.c GitHub (Karpathy)
pretraining_frameworks.relevance: Karpathy's minimal C/CUDA GPT-2 pre-training implementation. Educational reference; used in 'Let's reproduce GPT-2' video. Last push 2025-06-26 (verified 2026-08-31) — stable but not actively developed; expect toolchain drift against a current CUDA/PyTorch stack.

pretraining_frameworks.name: levanter GitHub (marin-community)
pretraining_frameworks.relevance: JAX/TPU pre-training framework from Stanford CRFM, now maintained under the Marin community project. The older stanford-crfm/levanter path 301-redirects here (verified 2026-08-31). Slower cadence than torchtitan/Megatron-LM: last push 2026-01-26.

pretraining_frameworks.name: nanochat GitHub (Karpathy)
pretraining_frameworks.relevance: Karpathy's end-to-end small-model train+chat reference loop; uses Muon. Actively developed, so preferred over llm.c as the executable GPT-2-scale reproduction target.

storage_and_data_pipeline.name: Chris Fregly, AI Systems Performance Engineering (O'Reilly, Nov 2025) — Ch. 5, GPU-Based Storage I/O Optimizations
storage_and_data_pipeline.relevance: Primary source for references/storage-and-dataloader-io.md: sequential-vs-random read layout, NVMe blk-mq and NFS client tuning, replication vs compression tradeoffs, GPUDirect Storage and gdsio benchmarking, cuda-checkpoint, dataloader-bound diagnosis, and the continuous profiling workflow.

storage_and_data_pipeline.name: NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage Documentation (cuFile, nvidia-fs, gdsio)
storage_and_data_pipeline.relevance: Authoritative GDS reference: cuFile API, supported filesystems and RDMA stacks, O_DIRECT requirements, and the gdsio benchmarking tool. Hardware/driver support drifts — verify requirements here rather than quoting a version.

storage_and_data_pipeline.name: NVIDIA DALI GitHub
storage_and_data_pipeline.relevance: GPU-accelerated data loading and preprocessing (JPEG/video decode, augmentation) for input-bound training. Reference for offloading dataloader CPU work to the GPU.

storage_and_data_pipeline.name: PyTorch DataLoader Reference
storage_and_data_pipeline.relevance: Canonical semantics for num_workers, pin_memory, prefetch_factor, persistent_workers, collate_fn, and DistributedSampler — the knobs used in the dataloader-bound diagnosis workflow.

storage_and_data_pipeline.name: DeepSeek 3FS (Fire-Flyer File System)
storage_and_data_pipeline.relevance: Open-source filesystem codesigned for AI random-read workloads: direct file I/O bypassing the page cache, RDMA-first data paths, sharded metadata. Reference point for storage codesign at ultrascale.

rented_gpu_providers.name: RunPod Pricing
rented_gpu_providers.relevance: Current RunPod GPU instance pricing including spot (interruptible) rates for A100, H100, and A10G. Verify before budgeting — prices change frequently.

rented_gpu_providers.name: Lambda Labs GPU Cloud Pricing
rented_gpu_providers.relevance: Lambda Labs on-demand and reserved GPU pricing. Often competitive for A100 clusters. Verify current rates; availability fluctuates.

rented_gpu_providers.name: Modal GPU Compute Pricing
rented_gpu_providers.relevance: Modal serverless GPU pricing. Per-second billing; good for short burst jobs and profiling runs. Supports H100 and A100 with simple Python SDK.
